title: Range Variety

source.name: Original exercise inspired by the classic distinct-values application of Mo's algorithm

statement:
A workshop logs one material code after each job. For each requested span of jobs, report how many different material codes appear in that span. Count each code once per span, even if it appears several times. The log stays fixed and all requests are available before you answer.

**Input.** The first line contains two integers, `n` and `q`. The second line contains the `n` material codes `a[1], ..., a[n]` in job order. Each of the next `q` lines contains two 1-indexed endpoints `l` and `r`, both included in the span.

**Output.** Print one integer per line for each request, in the order the requests were given.
hints: You can process the requests in any order if you save each answer at its original index.
When a window endpoint moves by one position, only one frequency changes. Track the number of values whose frequency is positive.
Group requests by the left endpoint's block of size floor(sqrt(n)). Sort each block by the right endpoint, ascending in even-numbered blocks and descending in odd-numbered blocks.
editorial:
### Order the queries

Apply **Mo's algorithm**. Compress the codes to consecutive IDs so equal codes share an ID and each frequency fits in an array. Convert each inclusive 1-indexed request `(l, r)` to the zero-indexed half-open interval `[l - 1, r)`. Save its original index.

Choose a block width `B = floor(sqrt(n))`. Sort by the block of the left endpoint. Within an even-numbered block, visit right endpoints in increasing order. Within an odd-numbered block, visit them in decreasing order. Alternating directions can reduce right-endpoint travel between blocks.

### Maintain the window

Start with the empty interval `[0, 0)`. Extend the current window to include the target interval, then shrink it to the exact target. On adding a code, increase the distinct count if its frequency changes from zero to one. On removing a code, decrease the count if its frequency changes from one to zero.

These updates keep each frequency equal to the number of occurrences of its code in the active window. The distinct count therefore equals the number of positive frequencies. Once the window has both target endpoints, save that count at the original query index. Print the saved counts in input order.

### Complexity

Left endpoints move at most `O(q B + n)` steps in total, since each move within a block covers at most `B` positions and the blocks advance in order. Right endpoints move at most `O(n ceil(n / B))` steps including transitions between blocks. Compression and sorting take `O(n log n + q log q)` time. With `B = floor(sqrt(n))`, the total time is `O(n log n + q log q + (n + q) sqrt(n))` and storage is `O(n + q)`.

Measured against `N = max(n, q)`, the intended Mo solution takes `O(N sqrt(N))` time and `O(N)` space.

solutions.python:
import sys
from math import isqrt

tokens = iter(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
n, q = next(tokens), next(tokens)
values = [next(tokens) for _ in range(n)]
ids = {value: i for i, value in enumerate(sorted(set(values)))}
values = [ids[value] for value in values]

block_size = isqrt(n)
queries = []
for index in range(q):
    left, right = next(tokens) - 1, next(tokens)
    block = left // block_size
    right_key = -right if block % 2 else right
    queries.append((block, right_key, left, right, index))
queries.sort()

freq = [0] * len(ids)
answers = [0] * q
lo = hi = distinct = 0
for _, _, left, right, index in queries:
    # The active window is [lo, hi).
    while lo > left:
        lo -= 1
        value = values[lo]
        if freq[value] == 0:
            distinct += 1
        freq[value] += 1
    while hi < right:
        value = values[hi]
        if freq[value] == 0:
            distinct += 1
        freq[value] += 1
        hi += 1
    while lo < left:
        value = values[lo]
        freq[value] -= 1
        if freq[value] == 0:
            distinct -= 1
        lo += 1
    while hi > right:
        hi -= 1
        value = values[hi]
        freq[value] -= 1
        if freq[value] == 0:
            distinct -= 1
    answers[index] = distinct

sys.stdout.write("\n".join(map(str, answers)) + "\n")
